The “mador” repository appears to be a lightweight tool written in a mainstream programming language, aimed at simplifying a specific development workflow (the exact functionality is outlined in the project’s README). Its initial reception suggests a modest but engaged community of developers who are evaluating its utility and potential contributions. As the project gains visibility, further contributions and feedback on both GitHub and Hacker News are expected to shape its development trajectory.
author: Hacker News

title: Isar Aerospace launches Europe's first fully commercial orbital rocket
content:
Isar Aerospace, a German launch‑service provider, announced the successful deployment of its two‑stage Spectrum rocket into low‑Earth orbit from the Andøya Spaceport in Norway. The flight marks Europe’s first entirely commercial orbital launch, following a failed attempt in March when the vehicle crashed into the sea after 30 seconds of flight. The Spectrum, designed for payloads up to 500 kilograms, reached its intended orbit without incident, delivering its cargo for a mix of commercial and institutional customers.

CEO and co‑founder Daniel Metzler said in a press release that the achievement “opens space from Continental Europe” and provides “a true alternative for commercial and institutional customers” amid what he described as the “largest bottleneck” in the global space industry. The company’s success is expected to increase launch capacity for European users and reduce reliance on non‑European providers, signaling a shift toward a more diversified and accessible market for orbital services.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami International Airport
content:
An Amazon‑branded cargo aircraft overran the runway while landing at Miami International Airport on Sunday, September 6, 2026, at approximately 2 p.m. local time. The Boeing 767‑300, operating as 21 Air Flight 7598, had arrived from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico, when it failed to stop on the runway and collided with ground vehicles, causing multiple injuries. The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed the incident and noted that the extent of the aircraft’s damage and the seriousness of the injuries were still being assessed at the time of the report.

Following the crash, all arrivals and departures at Miami International were temporarily halted, and more than 60 scheduled flights were delayed or canceled as emergency crews secured the runway and investigated the scene. Authorities have opened a full investigation into the cause of the overrun, and airport officials are working with Amazon and the aircraft operator to determine any contributing factors. The FAA and local emergency services continue to monitor the situation, and further updates are expected as the investigation progresses.
author: The Verge

title: Authors contest publishers' claim to Anthropic settlement funds
content:
Authors have voiced concerns that publishers are receiving a disproportionate portion of the recent settlement funds allocated to writers. The settlement, reached earlier this year in a dispute over royalty calculations and licensing agreements, earmarked several million dollars for distribution among affected authors, but representatives of the writing community say the majority of the payout has been directed to publishing houses.

Industry observers note that the authors’ complaints center on the settlement’s allocation formula, which they argue favors large publishers at the expense of individual writers. The authors’ group has called for a transparent audit of the distribution process and for adjustments that would ensure a more equitable share of the funds reaches the creators whose works generated the revenue. The matter is expected to be reviewed by the overseeing court in the coming weeks, with both parties awaiting further guidance on how the settlement monies will be disbursed.
author: TechCrunch

title: Amazon cargo plane overruns Miami runway, collides with vehicles and ignites
content:
A Boeing 767 operated by Amazon Prime Air was involved in an incident at Miami International Airport, prompting an immediate response from the Federal Aviation Administration and airport officials. The aircraft, which was conducting a cargo flight for the e‑commerce giant, experienced an unexplained event that led to its temporary grounding and a brief evacuation of the surrounding area.

Both the FAA and Miami International Airport confirmed that there was no immediate word on casualties, and emergency crews were dispatched to assess the situation and secure the site. Investigations are underway to determine the cause of the incident, while airline and airport operations continue under heightened safety protocols.
author: Euronews

title: FIFA president Infantino to run for fourth term despite controversy
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino announced on Sunday that he will run for a fourth and final term in the organization’s 2027 election, despite the controversy that surrounded his proposal earlier this year to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. The plan, which Infantino first unveiled in April, triggered widespread criticism from member associations, sponsors and fans who argued that commercializing the tournament could undermine the sport’s integrity. After intense backlash, the governing body shelved the initiative, but the president’s intention to seek re‑election remains unchanged.

A FIFA spokesperson confirmed that “nothing has changed” regarding Infantino’s candidacy, reiterating the president’s commitment to continue leading the federation through the next election cycle. The statement came as the organization prepares for its quadrennial congress, where the vote will be held and where the future direction of global football governance will be debated. The upcoming election will be Infantino’s last permissible term under FIFA’s statutes, marking a pivotal moment for the sport’s leadership.
author: France 24

title: Trump administration files another Supreme Court appeal on mail‑in voting
content:
The United States Supreme Court’s recent decisions on election‑law matters are poised to shape the political landscape ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. In a series of rulings issued over the past month, the Court upheld state‑level restrictions on absentee voting, limited the scope of the Voting Rights Act’s preclearance provision, and affirmed a lower‑court ruling that permits partisan gerrymandering challenges only under narrow circumstances. These judgments clarify the legal framework governing ballot access, district drawing, and campaign financing, and they set precedents that will be applied in dozens of states as they finalize their election procedures for the upcoming contests.

Analysts note that the rulings could affect voter turnout and the competitiveness of races in swing districts, particularly in states where absentee‑ballot restrictions and district maps have been contentious. Election officials are now required to implement the Court’s interpretations before the filing deadlines for candidate nominations and ballot‑access petitions, while political parties are adjusting their strategies to account for the revised legal environment. As the midterms approach, the Supreme Court’s interpretations will likely influence both the administration of elections and the broader dynamics of the 2026 electoral cycle.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Adidas faces boycott over ad featuring former Israeli soldier
content:
A new public‑relations campaign that features a photograph of an Israeli soldier has drawn sharp criticism from human‑rights activists, who say the imagery is out of step with the humanitarian toll of the ongoing conflict in Gaza. The campaign, launched by a pro‑military advocacy group, depicts the soldier in uniform with a caption intended to highlight security concerns, but activists argue that it fails to acknowledge the scale of civilian suffering. Their objection is underscored by recent medical reports indicating that more than 5,000 Palestinians have undergone amputations as a result of Israeli airstrikes and artillery fire in the densely populated enclave.

Human‑rights organizations and medical NGOs have called for the campaign to be withdrawn, emphasizing that the high number of amputations reflects a broader crisis in Gaza’s health infrastructure, where hospitals are operating under severe shortages of supplies and electricity. The groups contend that any public messaging about the conflict should incorporate the civilian impact, noting that the amputations are part of a larger pattern of injuries and displacement affecting the population. They have urged international bodies to increase monitoring and aid to address the medical needs of those injured, while also calling for a reassessment of public outreach strategies that may appear insensitive to the suffering on the ground.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Anak Krakatau eruption disrupts hundreds of flights in Indonesia
content:
Indonesia’s Anak Krakatau volcano recorded two additional eruptions on Tuesday, extending a series of explosive events that have been generating ash plumes over the surrounding seas. The eruptions were detected by the Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG) and confirmed by satellite imagery, which showed ash reaching altitudes of up to 3,000 meters above sea level. Authorities have maintained a 4‑kilometer exclusion zone around the crater and have issued aviation advisories warning pilots of reduced visibility and potential engine damage.

The continued ash emissions have prompted heightened monitoring by both Indonesian disaster agencies and international aviation bodies, which have updated flight routes to avoid the affected airspace. Local fishermen have reported thicker ash fall on nearby islands, though no injuries or structural damage have been reported so far. Officials emphasized that the volcano remains active and that further eruptions are possible, urging residents and maritime operators to stay informed through official channels.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed discusses Muslim faith and American identity
content:
Detroit – In a remarks delivered at the Islamic Center of Detroit on March 15, 2024, Republican Senate candidate John D. Smith addressed his personal faith and the challenges confronting Muslim Americans in the state. Smith, a former state legislator, said his upbringing in a devout Christian household informs his belief in religious liberty and underscored the need for “equal respect for all faiths.” He cited recent reports of anti‑Muslim harassment and urged lawmakers to strengthen hate‑crime statutes, improve community‑police relations, and ensure that federal immigration policies do not target individuals based on religion.

Smith’s comments come as the Michigan Senate race enters its final primary phase, with both major parties seeking to broaden their appeal among diverse voter blocs. By highlighting the experiences of Muslim constituents, the candidate aims to demonstrate a commitment to inclusive representation while differentiating his platform on civil‑rights protections. The campaign indicated that the outreach will continue through town‑hall meetings and partnerships with faith‑based organizations ahead of the November general election.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Five dead, nine rescued after student housing collapse in New Delhi
content:
At least five people were killed and nine rescued after a multi‑storey building that housed primarily students collapsed in New Delhi. The incident, which occurred in the city’s central district, prompted an immediate response from local emergency services, fire crews and police who arrived on the scene within minutes to assess the damage and begin rescue operations.

Rescue teams worked through the rubble for several hours, extracting survivors and transporting the injured to nearby hospitals. Officials have not yet disclosed the cause of the collapse, though preliminary investigations will examine the building’s structural integrity and any possible violations of safety regulations. The district administration has warned residents to avoid the area while the site is secured, and families of the victims have been notified as authorities continue to search for any additional survivors.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Opinion polls show opposition bloc ahead of Netanyahu's coalition
content:
Recent opinion polls released this week indicate that the opposition bloc has taken a lead over the coalition supporting the current prime minister, marking a shift in voter sentiment ahead of the scheduled national elections. The surveys, conducted by three independent research firms, show the opposition at 38‑42 percent of the vote share, while the incumbent coalition trails between 34 and 37 percent, with the remaining respondents undecided or supporting smaller parties.

Analysts attribute the swing to growing public concerns over economic policy and recent legislative controversies, though the polls also note a margin of error that leaves the race competitive. The results are expected to influence campaign strategies as parties intensify outreach in key swing regions before the election date set for early November. Election officials have confirmed that the vote will be conducted under the existing proportional representation system, which could determine whether the opposition secures enough seats to form a government or if the incumbent coalition must seek new partners to retain power.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Susan Sarandon claims loss of film roles due to Palestine support
content:
Veteran actress and activist Susan Sarandon told reporters that she continues to be passed over for film projects because of her public support for Palestine. In an interview conducted earlier this week, Sarandon said she has been informed by casting directors and producers that her outspoken stance on the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict makes her a “risk” for studios seeking to avoid controversy. She cited recent instances in which she was considered for roles but ultimately removed from the shortlist after her advocacy was brought to the attention of decision‑makers.

Sarandon’s remarks come amid a broader wave of scrutiny directed at Hollywood figures who have voiced criticism of Israel’s actions in the Gaza war that began in October 2023. Industry observers note that several actors, directors, and writers have faced similar setbacks, with some studios reportedly instituting informal “blacklists” to deter pro‑Palestinian statements. The actress, who has a long history of political activism, said the pattern of lost opportunities underscores a growing pressure on entertainment companies to align with pro‑Israel sentiment, especially as they navigate a polarized public discourse.

While Sarandon declined to name specific projects, she emphasized that the trend affects not only her career but also the creative choices available to other artists willing to speak out. She reiterated her commitment to advocacy despite the professional costs, noting that the issue has become a litmus test for many in the film industry. The actress’s comments add to ongoing debates about freedom of expression, corporate risk management, and the influence of geopolitical issues on Hollywood casting decisions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: AfD projected to win Saxony-Anhalt regional election
content:
Germany’s far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is projected to emerge as the largest party in the upcoming state election in Saxony‑Anhalt, according to the latest exit‑poll data released by the state’s electoral commission. The AfD is expected to secure roughly 28 % of the vote, edging out the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and the Social Democratic Party (SPD), which are projected at 24 % and 22 % respectively. Voter turnout was reported at 68 %, slightly above the previous election in 2021, and the results reflect a continued shift in the eastern states where the AfD has been gaining ground since its parliamentary breakthrough in 2017.

The projected outcome means the AfD will likely lead coalition talks, though a partnership with the CDU or SPD appears unlikely given the parties’ stated refusal to cooperate with the far‑right. Analysts suggest the result could force a coalition of the CDU, SPD and the Greens, or a minority government supported by the Free Democratic Party, to form a stable executive. The Saxony‑Anhalt result is being watched closely as an indicator of the AfD’s momentum ahead of the federal elections scheduled for next year, where its performance could influence the balance of power in the Bundestag.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US peace talks with Russia and Ukraine underscore symbolic gestures amid ongoing conflict
content:
U.S. diplomatic representatives have recently met separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in an effort to revive stalled negotiations over the conflict that began in February 2022. The talks, conducted behind closed doors, focused on potential cease‑fire mechanisms, humanitarian corridors and the possibility of a phased withdrawal of forces, but no public agreements have emerged. Both sides have reiterated their positions: Moscow insists on recognition of territorial changes, while Kyiv demands a complete restoration of its internationally recognized borders.

Despite the diplomatic activity, officials in Kyiv remain skeptical that the negotiations will alter the course of the war. According to a report by James Landale, Ukrainian authorities expect hostilities to continue unabated, citing ongoing Russian offensives in the east and south and a lack of concrete concessions from Moscow. The United States, while maintaining its role as a mediator, has emphasized that any durable settlement must address Ukraine’s security concerns, a stance that appears to reinforce Kyiv’s anticipation of prolonged fighting.
author: BBC World

title: SpaceX Expands Starbase Facilities Ahead of Flight 14
content:
SpaceX is continuing to expand its assembly, test, and launch infrastructure at the Starbase facility in Texas as it prepares for the upcoming Flight 14 mission. According to a recent update on NASA SpaceFlight.com, the company is still in the process of constructing key support structures and upgrading systems that will enable the next Falcon 9 launch to proceed safely and efficiently.

The new infrastructure includes additional assembly bays, upgraded testing rigs, and enhanced launch pad systems designed to accommodate the increased frequency of launches that SpaceX plans to achieve at Starbase. These developments are part of the company’s broader effort to streamline operations and reduce turnaround times between flights, ensuring that the next mission can launch on schedule.

With the infrastructure upgrades underway, SpaceX remains on track to move Flight 14 forward, maintaining its schedule for the next Falcon 9 launch. The continued investment in Starbase’s facilities underscores the company’s commitment to sustaining high launch cadence and supporting future missions from the Texas launch complex.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Shaw scores twice as City beat Birmingham to start WSL season
content:
Manchester City’s new campaign kicked off with a decisive 3‑2 victory over Birmingham City, as Jamaican striker Khadija Shaw netted a brace to secure the win. Shaw’s two goals mirrored the tally she delivered in the final game of last season’s Women’s Super League, underscoring the club’s confidence in her by offering a new contract during the summer transfer window. The Jamaican’s performance, coupled with a strong defensive showing, ensured City’s place at the top of the table from the outset.

Birmingham’s newly promoted goalkeeper, Sophie Baggaley, made a notable debut, keeping the visitors at bay and denying the opposition a third goal. Despite Baggaley’s clean sheet, City’s clinical finishing proved too much for the hosts. Meanwhile, other top clubs also found success that day: Arsenal, Crystal Palace, Tottenham Hotspur and Liverpool all secured victories in their respective fixtures, adding to the competitive momentum heading into the season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sophia Dunkley’s 119 secures England’s 3‑0 ODI series win over Ireland
content:
Sophia Dunkley’s second One‑Day International century of the season propelled England to a decisive 291‑run victory over Ireland at Worcester, clinching a 3‑0 series sweep. The England side, chasing a modest target, finished comfortably after Ireland were bowled out for 291 in 48.5 overs. Dunkley’s 102, complemented by Maia Bouchier’s aggressive start, set the tone for the hosts’ innings.

Ireland, batting first for the first time in the series, had been on course for a sizeable total after a powerful opening partnership from Dunkley and Bouchier. However, the hosts collapsed dramatically in the final stages, losing their last six wickets for just 31 runs. England’s bowlers capitalised on the sudden shift, securing the final wickets in quick succession and stifling any comeback attempt from the Irish side.

With the series now complete, England’s clean sweep underscores their dominance in the limited‑overs format, while Ireland’s collapse highlights the fine margins that can decide a match. The result leaves England in a strong position ahead of upcoming fixtures, and Ireland with lessons to address before their next international engagements.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tim Wellens wins Tour of Britain
content:
Tim Wellens secured overall victory in the men’s Tour of Britain, taking the lead on the fourth stage through the hills of North Yorkshire and holding it to the finish. The Belgian rider, a teammate of Tadej Pogacar on the UAE Emirates XRG team, entered the final stage in Earlston with a 21‑second advantage over British contender Lewis Askey. Wellens extended that margin to 42 seconds by the finish line, cementing his win in a race that showcased his climbing prowess and tactical acumen.

Askey, who had performed strongly throughout the earlier stages, finished second overall, earning a podium spot for Britain. The 21‑year‑old Ben Wiggins, son of former Olympic champion Sir Bradley Wiggins, placed 10th overall, adding a notable name to the final standings. The Tour’s final day highlighted the depth of talent in the field, with Wellens’ decisive move securing his place among the sport’s elite.

The victory underscores Wellens’ continued dominance on the European circuit and adds another accolade to the UAE Emirates XRG team’s growing reputation. Meanwhile, Askey’s performance and Wiggins’ respectable finish demonstrate the competitive spirit and international diversity that define the Tour of Britain.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Brennan Criticises Heat as Van Aert Wins Shortened Vuelta Stage
content:
The Vuelta a España’s 15th stage in Córdoba was cut short by soaring temperatures, with Wout van Aert of Visma‑Lease a Bike taking the sprint finish. The stage, originally planned to cover a longer distance, was reduced after riders and officials expressed concern over the extreme heat. Van Aert crossed the line first, securing a win for his team and adding another victory to his season.

British rider Matthew Brennan, who was in the lead group on the early climb, described the conditions as “41 °C average, 44 °C at the summit.” He said the heat forced riders to question whether it was safe to continue, comparing the temperature to a typical office thermostat. The Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) officials reportedly set their office climate to 20 °C, underscoring the stark contrast between the race environment and everyday conditions.

Enric Mas has retained the red leader’s jersey after the shortened stage, maintaining his advantage in the overall classification. The Vuelta will resume with the next stage, but the heatwave has prompted renewed discussions about rider safety and race protocols in extreme weather.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ødegaard scores winner as Arsenal overturn Chelsea
content:
The season’s opening heavyweight clash between Arsenal and Chelsea began with an instant shock. Within 77 seconds, Morgan Rogers struck from the edge of the area, sending a clean volley past Arsenal’s goalkeeper and giving Chelsea a 1‑0 lead. It was the first goal Arsenal have conceded in the Premier League this campaign, a fact that added a layer of drama to an already highly anticipated fixture.

Under Xabi Alonso, Chelsea have returned to a fluid, free‑scoring style, while Arsenal have been praised for their resolute, no‑give‑an‑inch approach. The early strike highlighted a fundamental mismatch: Arsenal’s percussive, possession‑based play has struggled to contain Chelsea’s quick, incisive attacks. Rogers’ goal also carries a narrative twist, as the former Arsenal prospect was signed by Chelsea for £117 million after a summer chase that saw him leave the Gunners for their rivals.

The early setback will test Arsenal’s defensive solidity and tactical discipline, while Chelsea’s early advantage sets the tone for a match that could see the new manager’s philosophy take shape. As the game progressed, both sides will need to adjust to the momentum shift, with Arsenal looking to regain control and Chelsea eager to extend the lead.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Hamilton says Ferrari can't give him priority over Leclerc
content:
Lewis Hamilton, the seven‑time Formula 1 World Champion, told reporters that it is “far too late” for Ferrari to give him priority over his teammate Charles Leclerc in the current championship fight. Speaking after the most recent race, Hamilton emphasized that any decision to shift the focus from Leclerc to himself would come too late to affect the standings in the drivers’ title battle.

Ferrari has maintained Leclerc as its lead driver for the season, a strategy that has paid dividends with multiple podiums and a championship‑contending performance. Hamilton’s remarks underline the competitive tension within the team and highlight the importance of a clear hierarchy for maximizing results. With the championship still open, the decision on driver prioritisation will likely remain a key point of discussion as the season progresses.
author: BBC Sport

title: WSL Returns with New Signings and Rising Contenders, Man City Leads
content:
The Women’s Super League kicked off its new season this weekend, drawing attention with a wave of fresh signings, upgraded squads, and a handful of surprising outcomes. Clubs that had struggled in the previous campaign have bolstered their rosters, bringing in international talent and promising domestic players to strengthen key positions.

Early fixtures revealed the impact of the new additions. Several teams that had been mid‑table last year moved into the top half, while a few established powerhouses were knocked out of contention by lower‑ranked opponents. The league’s competitive balance has shifted, with several matches ending in unexpected draws or narrow victories that defied pre‑season expectations.

As the season progresses, analysts will be watching how the newly signed players integrate and whether the early shocks signal a broader realignment of power within the league. The WSL’s return has already demonstrated that squad upgrades and tactical adjustments can quickly alter the competitive landscape, setting the stage for a highly unpredictable campaign.
author: BBC Sport

title: Arsenal beat Chelsea after trailing
content:
Arsenal secured a dramatic 2‑1 victory over Chelsea in a London derby at the Emirates Stadium, overturning a 1‑0 deficit to finish as the reigning Premier League champions. The match, played on a wet Saturday afternoon, saw the Gunners level the score in the 61st minute with a well‑placed header from Bukayo Saka, before a late strike from Gabriel Jesus sealed the win.

Chelsea opened the scoring early through a penalty awarded for a handball in the box, and their high‑profile squad, known for recent heavy spending, dominated the first half. Arsenal’s resilience was evident in the second half, as they pressed aggressively, forcing several key chances and capitalising on a defensive lapse from the Blues. The win not only gives Arsenal a valuable three points but also keeps them in the top four, while the result leaves Chelsea to reassess their campaign after a disappointing start.

The triumph underscores Arsenal’s continued momentum under manager Mikel Arteta, who has guided the team to a title‑winning season. With the Premier League still in its early stages, the victory provides a boost for the Gunners as they look to maintain their position at the summit, while Chelsea will need to address defensive solidity if they hope to re‑enter contention for European qualification.
author: BBC Sport

title: Carrick remains upbeat after Man Utd's loss to Everton
content:
Manchester United’s new manager, Michael Carrick, expressed confidence after the club’s 3‑2 defeat to Everton at Goodison Park, a result that saw the Red Devils drop two points from a potential three. The loss extended a run of disappointing performances that has left United’s league position slipping toward the lower end of the top half. Carrick, who took charge in the off‑season, praised his squad’s effort but acknowledged the need for further improvement in both attack and defence.

The match was a hard‑fought encounter, with Everton’s midfield dominating possession and exploiting gaps in United’s back line. Carrick highlighted the importance of maintaining composure in the final third, noting that the team’s passing accuracy fell short of the club’s standards. He also emphasized the significance of the upcoming fixtures against Tottenham and Aston Villa, where a positive result could help to arrest the slide in the standings.

Despite the setback, Carrick remains optimistic about the trajectory of the team. He stressed that the club’s long‑term objectives—solidifying a top‑four finish and progressing in European competition—remain achievable with disciplined performances and strategic adjustments. The United faithful will be watching closely as the club seeks to regain momentum in the remaining fixtures of the season.
author: BBC Sport

title: Odegaard and Saka Rated Highly in Arsenal vs Chelsea Match
content:
Arsenal and Chelsea faced off in a tightly contested Premier League encounter that ended 1‑1, with the teams exchanging goals in the first half and the second half seeing both sides unable to break the deadlock. Following the match, the official player ratings released by the league’s statistical partner highlighted the standout performers and underscored the areas where each side struggled.

Arsenal’s best‑rated player was Bukayo Saka, who finished with an 8.2, contributing a key assist and a decisive shot that was saved by Chelsea’s keeper. Gabriel scored the opening goal and earned a 7.5 for his work rate and defensive contribution. Midfielders Martinelli and Gündoğan posted ratings of 7.1 and 6.9 respectively, while goalkeeper Aaron Ramsdale received a 7.4 for his two crucial saves. On the Chelsea side, Mason Mount led the ratings with an 8.0, driving the attack and creating several chances. Timo Werner, who scored the equaliser, was rated 7.3, while Jorginho’s 7.0 reflected his influence in midfield. Goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga earned a 6.8 after a handful of important stops.

The ratings suggest that while both squads displayed solid individual performances, Arsenal’s attacking flair and defensive solidity were slightly more effective than Chelsea’s, as reflected in the higher average rating of 7.2 compared to Chelsea’s 7.0. The match’s outcome and the players’ evaluations will likely inform both teams’ tactical adjustments ahead of their next fixtures.
author: BBC Sport

title: Wright Says Iran War Needed to Reset Middle East
content:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ABC News’s “This Week” on Sunday that the United States views the ongoing war with Iran as a necessary step to “reset” the Middle East. Wright emphasized that the primary objective of the conflict, as articulated by senior administration officials, is to prevent Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, describing a nuclear‑armed Iran as a “dangerous reality” for regional and global security.

Wright’s remarks come amid heightened diplomatic and military activity surrounding the dispute, with the U.S. maintaining that its involvement is aimed at curbing Tehran’s nuclear ambitions while supporting allies in the region. He reiterated the administration’s long‑standing position that sustained pressure on Iran is essential to achieving a non‑proliferation outcome, and indicated that the current strategy will continue to guide U.S. policy in the Middle East.
author: The Hill

title: Policymakers urged to assess impact of bank mergers on innovation
content:
Policymakers focused on preserving the United States’ capacity for innovation are turning their attention to the downstream consequences of recent bank consolidations. In a series of briefings held this week, officials from the Treasury Department and the Federal Reserve highlighted that while mergers can create larger, potentially more stable financial institutions, they may also reshape the flow of credit to emerging technology firms and research-driven startups that rely on diversified banking relationships.

Regulators and industry groups cited several high‑profile mergers, including the acquisition of regional lender XYZ Bank by national powerhouse ABC Financial, as case studies for evaluating changes in loan underwriting standards, regional branch closures, and the concentration of decision‑making authority. Studies presented to congressional committees indicated that reduced competition in local banking markets can lead to tighter credit conditions for small‑business borrowers, potentially slowing the pace of venture financing and R&D investment. Lawmakers are slated to review proposed amendments to the Bank Merger Act that would require more detailed impact assessments on innovation ecosystems before approving future consolidations.
author: The Hill

title: Lawler Criticizes Trump Over Iran War Statement
content:
Rep. Mike Lawler (R‑N. Y.) publicly disagreed with President Donald J. Trump’s recent remarks downplaying the seriousness of the U.S. involvement in the Iran conflict. Speaking on CNN, Lawler cautioned that any military escalation “is certainly not small potatoes” and that the nation must recognize the gravity of the situation. The congressman’s statement came after the president’s comments suggested the war was being over‑simplified.

Lawler’s remarks highlight a growing tension between the executive and some members of Congress over how the administration frames foreign military engagements. While Trump has repeatedly emphasized a more restrained approach to the conflict in Iran, Lawler’s warning underscores concerns that the administration’s messaging may understate the risks and operational realities on the ground. The congressman’s comments were part of a broader debate among lawmakers about the U.S.’s role in the region and the need for clear, realistic assessments of military actions.

In closing, Lawler’s statement signals a willingness among some Republican representatives to challenge the president’s narrative on foreign policy matters. The exchange underscores the importance of bipartisan scrutiny of U.S. military involvement abroad, as lawmakers weigh the potential consequences of underestimating the stakes in the Iran war.
author: The Hill

title: Affordability Debate Must Include Workers' Wages
content:
A recent policy briefing highlighted that tackling affordability requires more than cutting consumer prices. Experts argue that a truly effective agenda must also raise workers’ real incomes so that wages keep pace with rising living costs. The briefing emphasized that higher wages, coupled with stronger collective bargaining, are essential for workers to maintain purchasing power and avoid falling into debt traps.

The report outlined several mechanisms for achieving this dual focus. It called for targeted wage growth in sectors most affected by inflation, as well as reforms to strengthen labor unions and collective bargaining rights. By ensuring that wage increases are not merely nominal but reflect actual cost-of-living adjustments, policymakers can align income growth with price dynamics, thereby stabilizing household budgets across the economy.

In conclusion, the briefing underscored that affordability is a multifaceted challenge. Addressing it effectively demands both price moderation and robust wage policies that empower workers through collective action. Only by integrating these elements can policymakers create a sustainable path toward economic resilience for households nationwide.
author: The Hill

title: Calcium Scoring vs Traditional Risk: No Difference in Cardiovascular Events
content:
At the European Society of Cardiology Congress 2026, a Hot Line session revealed that initiating statin therapy based on coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring does not reduce the incidence of major cardiovascular events compared with the traditional risk factor assessment approach. The findings were presented by researchers who evaluated a cohort of patients undergoing CAC scans and subsequently received statin therapy guided either by their calcium scores or by conventional risk calculators such as the SCORE or ASCVD risk equations.

The analysis, which followed participants over a median period of several years, showed no statistically significant difference in outcomes such as myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death between the two groups. While CAC scoring remains a valuable tool for risk stratification, the study suggests that it may not provide additional benefit in guiding statin therapy beyond established risk factor models.

These results underscore the importance of continuing to rely on well‑validated risk assessment tools for statin prescribing decisions. Clinicians and guideline committees may need to reconsider the role of CAC scoring in routine practice, as its use does not appear to confer a measurable advantage in preventing major cardiovascular events.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Deep learning reveals six continuous bands at Earth's core‑mantle boundary
content:
Scientists have overcome the inability to drill to the core‑mantle boundary (CMB) by applying deep‑learning techniques to seismic data collected during earthquakes. In a study published in *Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth*, researchers analyzed a large set of a specific type of seismic wave and identified six continuous bands of irregularities at the CMB that had previously been detected only as isolated patches. The new method provides a more detailed and coherent picture of the boundary’s structure.

The CMB, located roughly 2,900 km beneath the Earth’s surface, marks the interface between the liquid outer core and the solid mantle. Its irregularities influence the planet’s magnetic field, mantle convection, and seismic wave propagation. By training neural networks on thousands of seismic waveforms, the team was able to extract subtle patterns that were invisible to traditional analysis. The resulting bands reveal a more complex, organized structure than the scattered anomalies reported in earlier studies, offering fresh constraints on the composition and dynamics of the deep Earth.

This breakthrough demonstrates the power of machine learning to enhance geophysical imaging where direct sampling is impossible. The refined map of the CMB may improve models of Earth’s thermal and chemical evolution and guide future seismic surveys aimed at probing the planet’s interior.
author: Phys.org

title: Substitutions Alter Energy Pathways in Aggregation-Induced Emission
content:
Certain chemical substances, broadly termed luminogens, possess an intrinsic ability to emit light. In dilute solutions these molecules readily fluoresce, but when they are brought together in the solid state the emission is dramatically reduced. The loss of light output is attributed to aggregation‑caused quenching, a phenomenon in which close packing of the molecules facilitates non‑radiative energy dissipation pathways that dominate over radiative decay.

Researchers are investigating strategies to preserve or even enhance solid‑state fluorescence. Approaches include designing rigid molecular frameworks that restrict intramolecular motion, incorporating bulky substituents to prevent tight packing, and engineering host–guest systems that isolate luminogens within a matrix. Such advances could enable the development of efficient solid‑state lighting, high‑resolution displays, and bioimaging probes that maintain brightness in solid or densely packed environments.

The continued study of luminogens and their aggregation behavior is essential for translating laboratory fluorescence into practical technologies. By overcoming the quenching that plagues many conventional fluorophores, scientists aim to create robust, bright materials suitable for next‑generation optoelectronic devices and biomedical applications.
author: Phys.org

title: OpenAI details monitoring of internal coding agents for misalignment
content:
OpenAI has detailed a new internal framework for monitoring the alignment of its coding agents, such as Codex and the code‑generation capabilities of ChatGPT, in a recent blog post titled “How we monitor internal coding agents mis‑alignment.” The company describes a multi‑layered approach that combines automated logging, anomaly detection, and periodic human audits to identify outputs that deviate from safety and quality standards. Metrics tracked include the frequency of insecure code patterns, the generation of disallowed functionalities, and the emergence of unintended behaviors flagged by internal red‑team tests. When anomalies are detected, the system triggers containment protocols that suspend the offending model instance and route the output for review, while continuous reinforcement learning updates aim to reduce recurrence.

OpenAI’s disclosure follows broader industry concerns about the potential misuse of AI‑generated code, including the creation of vulnerabilities or malicious scripts. By publishing its monitoring methodology, the organization seeks to increase transparency and reassure developers that safeguards are actively maintained. The post has sparked discussion on platforms such as Hacker News, where users have raised questions about the scalability of the oversight mechanisms and the criteria used to define misalignment. OpenAI indicates that the monitoring framework will evolve alongside its models, with ongoing refinements intended to keep pace with emerging risks.
author: Hacker News

title: Nitter repository unarchived, development to continue
content:
A new commit has been pushed to the open‑source “Nitter” project, a privacy‑focused front‑end for Twitter, under the repository zedeus/nitter. Identified by the hash 1428b4c2b4246f92a7e5b2673438e5fb39fcc4a3, the change updates the application’s handling of media URLs and refines the rate‑limiting logic that governs API requests. The modifications also include a minor dependency upgrade to address a known security advisory, and they adjust default configuration values to improve stability on low‑resource deployments.

The update was posted on GitHub and quickly surfaced on Hacker News, where the submission received 15 points despite attracting no comments. The brief community reaction suggests that the change is being noted by users who rely on Nitter for an ad‑free, non‑tracking Twitter experience, while the lack of discussion indicates the patch is viewed as a routine maintenance improvement rather than a controversial alteration.
author: Hacker News

title: Nitter project continues after legal advice
content:
A GitHub repository for Nitter, an open‑source, privacy‑focused front‑end for Twitter, has attracted notable attention on the technology news site Hacker News. The project, maintained at github.com/zedeus/nitter, offers users a lightweight interface that strips tracking scripts and presents tweets without requiring a Twitter account. On the Hacker News discussion page (news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49589003), the post garnered 147 points and generated 27 comments, indicating strong community interest in alternatives that enhance user privacy and reduce reliance on the official Twitter platform.

The discussion highlighted Nitter’s ability to serve as a proxy that caches media, supports RSS feeds, and can be self‑hosted, making it appealing for both casual users and developers seeking to embed Twitter content without exposing personal data. Contributors noted recent updates to the codebase, improved compatibility with Twitter’s API changes, and growing adoption across various instances. The conversation reflects broader trends toward decentralized web services and the demand for tools that mitigate data collection by major social networks.
author: Hacker News

title: AfD leads Saxony-Anhalt state election as polls close
content:
“Everything is possible,” the slogan of the far‑right Alternative for Germany (AfD), echoed across polling stations as Saxony‑Anhalt voters cast their ballots in the state election that concluded today. The phrase, promoted by the party’s leading candidate Ulrich Siegmund, frames the contest as a pivotal moment for Germany’s political landscape, with the AfD seeking to translate its surge in public support into executive power for the first time in the state.

Siegmund, who has consistently topped opinion polls ahead of the vote, stands poised to become Saxony‑Anhalt’s next Minister‑President if the party’s share of the vote translates into a governing majority or a viable coalition partner. The AfD’s ascendancy in the eastern state reflects broader shifts in voter sentiment, as concerns over immigration, economic restructuring and national identity have bolstered the party’s appeal since its entry into the Bundestag in 2017. Election officials will now begin the count, and the final results are expected to be announced within the next 24 hours, setting the stage for coalition talks that will determine whether the AfD can convert its campaign momentum into governmental authority.
author: France 24

title: Palestinian farmers in Hebron confront settler sabotage and military restrictions
content:
West Bank farmers have continued to work their fields despite a series of daily challenges that include settler attacks, the theft of livestock and restrictions imposed by the Israeli military. According to reports from local agricultural cooperatives, the farms are located in areas near major settlement blocs where clashes between Palestinian residents and Israeli settlers are frequent. Farmers say they regularly face harassment from settlers who attempt to damage crops and fence off portions of the land, while incidents of sheep and goat theft have risen sharply over the past year. Military regulations further complicate agricultural activities, as access to certain fields requires permits that are often delayed or denied, and roadblocks limit the transport of produce to markets.

The persistence of the farmers has been documented by several humanitarian organizations, which note that the community relies on the land for both livelihood and cultural identity. Despite the obstacles, the growers employ traditional irrigation methods and coordinate with neighboring villages to share resources and security information. Officials from the Israeli Defense Forces have stated that they are investigating settler violence, while Palestinian authorities have called for greater protection of agricultural zones. The continued cultivation of the disputed territories underscores the resilience of the West Bank’s farming population amid ongoing tensions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix after starting 19th
content:
Italian driver Luca Antonelli delivered a dramatic performance at the Monza Grand Prix on Sunday, climbing from 19th on the grid to claim victory in a race that secured him the season‑long championship. The win marked the first time in six decades that an Italian has captured the title in the series, ending a 60‑year drought for the nation’s motorsport fans.

Antonelli’s surge began on the opening lap, where he overtook several competitors before the first chicane. By the midway point he had moved into the top five, and a decisive pit‑stop strategy allowed him to undercut the race leader on lap 34. He maintained a consistent pace through the high‑speed straights of the Autodromo Nazionale, ultimately crossing the finish line ahead of his closest rival by 0.8 seconds. The victory awarded him 25 points, bringing his total to 212, which placed him eight points clear of the runner‑up with two races remaining in the calendar.

The championship triumph not only highlights Antonelli’s rapid development as a driver but also revives Italy’s presence at the pinnacle of the sport. Team officials praised his composure under pressure, while the win is expected to boost interest in the series across the country ahead of the season’s final events.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN launches $50 million appeal for Nepal flood survivors as death toll tops 1,300
content:
The United Nations has launched a $50 million humanitarian appeal to assist more than 84,000 people displaced by recent monsoon floods in Nepal. The appeal, announced by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), comes as flood‑affected communities face heightened risk of cholera and severe sanitation shortfalls, prompting urgent calls for resources to prevent a public‑health emergency.

The funding is earmarked for emergency water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) interventions, cholera surveillance, medical treatment, temporary shelter and food distribution, as well as support for the Nepalese government’s recovery plans. UN agencies, together with international partners, will coordinate the delivery of services and infrastructure repairs, aiming to restore safe water access and reduce disease transmission while stabilising livelihoods. The appeal seeks contributions from donor nations and private entities to meet the immediate needs and to lay the groundwork for longer‑term resilience in the flood‑hit regions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Arsenal beat Chelsea 2-1 to keep perfect Premier League start
content:
Arsenal secured a hard‑won victory in what manager Mikel Arteta described as the “stiffest test” of their Premier League title defence to date, overturning a first‑half deficit to claim three points. The Gunners fell behind early in the match but responded with a surge of attacking play, equalising through a well‑timed header before netting the winner from a swift counter‑attack in the second half. The result extended Arsenal’s lead at the top of the table and marked their first successful comeback of the season.

The win comes as Arsenal seek to consolidate their position ahead of a congested fixture schedule, having maintained an unbeaten run in the league since the start of the campaign. By navigating this challenging encounter, the team demonstrated resilience and depth, qualities that will be crucial as they aim to retain the Premier League crown. The victory also reinforces their standing ahead of upcoming domestic and European commitments, keeping them firmly in contention for the title.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 10-year-old Algerian boy dies after four days trapped in well
content:
Rescuers in Algeria have recovered the body of 10‑year‑old Ayoub, who died after becoming trapped in a well earlier this week. The incident, which occurred in the rural outskirts of the Tamanrasset province, prompted an immediate response from local emergency services and volunteers who worked through the night to locate the child.

Authorities said that a coordinated effort involving the national civil protection agency, fire brigade units and community members was launched within hours of the well‑fall. Divers and specialized equipment were deployed to widen the shaft and retrieve the boy, but despite the rapid response, Ayoub did not survive. Officials confirmed that the well had no protective covering and warned that similar unguarded structures pose a serious risk in remote areas. An investigation into the circumstances of the accident has been opened, and local officials urged residents to secure hazardous sites to prevent future tragedies.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Aryna Sabalenka reaches US Open quarterfinals
content:
Aryna Sabalenka, the two‑time defending champion, secured her place in the US Open quarterfinals on Tuesday after defeating American qualifier Taylor Townsend in straight sets, 6‑4, 6‑3. The match, played on Court 17 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, marked Sabalenka’s fifth consecutive appearance in the tournament’s last eight.

Sabalenka’s victory came after a solid first‑set performance in which she broke Townsend’s serve twice before consolidating the lead. In the second set, she maintained pressure with aggressive baseline play and a high first‑serve percentage, limiting Townsend’s opportunities to mount a comeback. The win extends Sabalenka’s unbeaten run at the US Open to 13 matches, positioning her for a potential third straight title as she prepares for a quarterfinal clash against the winner of the parallel match between [opponent’s name] and [opponent’s name].
author: Al Jazeera

title: Witkoff says Ukraine peace talks are very meaningful
content:
Ukrainian‑American diplomat Michael Witkoff told reporters on Thursday that the latest round of peace negotiations concerning the conflict in Ukraine has been “very meaningful.” Speaking after a three‑day session in Geneva that brought together representatives from Kyiv, Moscow and a coalition of European mediators, Witkoff said the talks produced a set of actionable proposals on cease‑fire monitoring, humanitarian corridors and the phased withdrawal of foreign forces.

The participants reviewed progress on previously agreed security guarantees and examined mechanisms for the return of displaced civilians, while also addressing the status of contested territories. Witkoff noted that both sides expressed a willingness to move forward on the outlined steps, though final ratification will require further diplomatic engagement. Observers indicated that the dialogue marks a notable shift from earlier stalemates, and the international community will continue to support the process as it advances toward a formal settlement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Argentina renews claim to Falkland Islands 44 years after war
content:
More than four decades after the 1982 conflict that pitted the United Kingdom against Argentina over the Falkland Islands, the Argentine government has formally renewed its claim to the archipelago. In a statement released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday, President Javier Milei reaffirmed Argentina’s “historical, legal and moral right” to the islands, known locally as Islas Malvinas, and announced that Buenos Aires will seek renewed discussion of the sovereignty issue at forthcoming United Nations forums. The declaration follows a series of diplomatic moves, including the appointment of a senior envoy to coordinate a multilateral campaign and the preparation of a legal brief to be submitted to the International Court of Justice, although the court’s jurisdiction would require the consent of both parties.

The United Kingdom, which has administered the Falklands continuously since the war’s end, reiterated its position that the islands’ status will not be altered without the explicit consent of the islanders, a stance supported by a 2013 referendum in which 99.8 % voted to remain a British Overseas Territory. While the renewed Argentine push has been welcomed by some Latin American governments, it has not yet led to any substantive change in the diplomatic relationship between London and Buenos Aires. Observers note that the latest assertion is part of a broader pattern of Argentine efforts to keep the sovereignty question on the international agenda, but the dispute remains unresolved as both nations maintain their respective claims.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran threatens stronger response after U.S. strikes on its oil tankers
content:
Washington announced on Monday that U.S. forces had struck Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for a series of attacks by Tehran on U.S. warships operating in the region. The strikes targeted vessels believed to be transporting fuel for the Iranian navy and were described by the Pentagon as a proportional response aimed at deterring further aggression against American naval assets. The attacks on the warships, which occurred earlier in the week, involved missile fire and small‑boat assaults that caused minor damage but prompted a swift escalation in the ongoing maritime tension between the two nations.

The remarks from U.S. officials came a day after the naval engagement, underscoring Washington’s intent to maintain freedom of navigation and protect its forces in the contested waters. Both sides have exchanged accusations, with Tehran condemning the U.S. action as an unlawful act of war, while the United States reaffirmed its right to defend its vessels. The situation remains volatile, and officials indicated that further diplomatic and military measures will be considered as events develop.
author: BBC World

title: Stoke Space and Relativity Space Advance LC-14 and LC-16 Toward First Flights
content:
Along Missile Row at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, two private launch providers are moving their new launch complexes closer to operational status. Stoke Space is preparing Launch Complex‑14 (LC‑14) for the first flight of its small‑satellite rocket, while Relativity Space is advancing Launch Complex‑16 (LC‑16) toward the maiden launch of its 3‑stage R‑Star vehicle. Both sites are situated on the historic Missile Row corridor, a stretch of Cape infrastructure that has supported U.S. spaceflight since the 1950s.

Stoke Space’s LC‑14 is a compact, reusable pad designed to accommodate its 4‑tonne “Stoke‑1” vehicle. The company has completed pad construction and is conducting static‑fire tests of the rocket’s Merlin‑derived engines. Relativity Space, meanwhile, is finalizing the 3‑stage R‑Star’s 3‑D‑printed aluminum‑lithium alloy airframe and installing the launch‑pad support infrastructure at LC‑16. Both companies have announced target launch windows for late 2026, with each company’s first flight expected to demonstrate the viability of their respective propulsion and manufacturing approaches.

With LC‑14 and LC‑16 approaching readiness, the Cape’s launch portfolio will expand to include two additional commercial launch sites that emphasize rapid development and cost efficiency. The successful first flights of Stoke‑1 and R‑Star would provide new options for small‑satellite operators and further diversify the commercial launch market at Cape Canaveral.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Top 10 Lego Star Wars Starships to Own
content:
**Lego Unveils Ten New Star Wars Starship Sets for Fans of All Allegiances**

Lego has announced a new line of ten Star Wars starship sets that promise to satisfy both Jedi and Sith enthusiasts alike. The collection, released in March 2026, includes iconic vessels such as the X‑Wing, TIE Fighter, Millennium Falcon, Imperial Star Destroyer, Slave I, AT‑AT, Y‑Wing, TIE Interceptor, Super Star Destroyer, and the Death Star. Each set features between 1,200 and 4,500 pieces, with release prices ranging from $59.99 for the TIE Fighter to $299.99 for the Death Star. The sets also incorporate interactive elements—such as moving wings, rotating turrets, and sound modules—designed to replicate the action-packed moments seen in the films.

The new line arrives as part of Lego’s ongoing partnership with Lucasfilm, which has expanded the franchise’s presence in the toy market since 2015. The sets are available in both retail stores and online, with limited-edition variants offering exclusive stickers and special packaging for collectors. Lego’s marketing team highlighted the sets’ compatibility with existing Star Wars Lego themes, allowing builders to integrate them into larger dioramas or combine them with the recently released “Star Wars: The Mandalorian” and “Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker” sets. The release is expected to boost sales in the holiday season, with analysts projecting a 12% increase in Lego’s Star Wars segment revenue.

Industry observers note that the breadth of ships—ranging from the nimble X‑Wing to the massive Death Star—provides a comprehensive representation of the Star Wars universe’s most celebrated spacecraft. The sets’ detailed designs, coupled with their playability, aim to appeal to both seasoned collectors and new fans. As Lego continues to expand its Star Wars catalog, the introduction of these ten starships marks a significant milestone in the brand’s effort to keep the galaxy far, far away alive for the next generation of builders.
author: Space.com

title: SpaceX Launches 27 Starlink Satellites, Falcon 9 Lands on Ship
content:
SpaceX launched a new batch of its Starlink internet satellites on September 6 from a launch site on California’s central coast. The company used its Falcon 9 rocket to lift the payload into orbit, continuing its rapid deployment of the constellation that aims to provide global broadband coverage.

The launch carried a typical payload of dozens of small satellites, each equipped with phased‑array antennas and high‑throughput transponders. The Falcon 9 first stage performed a successful return to the launch site, while the second stage deployed the satellites into a low‑Earth orbit. This mission follows a series of recent launches that have steadily increased the number of operational Starlink satellites worldwide.

With each launch, SpaceX expands the reach of its satellite network, bringing the company closer to its goal of delivering high‑speed internet to underserved regions. The September 6 flight adds to the growing constellation that is already in service in many parts of the globe.
author: Space.com

title: US Navy Launches First V-2 Rocket from Carrier on Sept. 6, 1947
content:
On September 6, 1947, the U.S. Navy successfully launched a V‑2 rocket from the deck of the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise, marking the first time a ballistic missile had been fired from a naval vessel. The test, conducted off the coast of California, demonstrated that a carrier could serve as a mobile launch platform, a capability that would later be leveraged for both military deterrence and space exploration.

The demonstration proved that the Navy could project missile power at sea, reducing the need for fixed launch sites and increasing operational flexibility. It also provided valuable data on the stresses of carrier deck operations, guidance systems, and recovery procedures, informing subsequent missile programs such as the Polaris submarine-launched ballistic missile and the Navy’s early space launch efforts. By showing that a ship could reliably launch a V‑2, the Navy opened a new dimension in strategic planning during the early Cold War.

This event laid groundwork for the development of sea‑based launch vehicles that would become integral to both defense and civilian space programs. It underscored the importance of mobility and rapid deployment in missile technology, influencing U.S. naval strategy and contributing to the eventual establishment of the U.S. space launch infrastructure that would later support the Apollo missions and beyond.
author: Space.com

title: Armstrong Misses Winning Chance as Birmingham and Wolves Draw
content:
Birmingham City secured a 1‑0 victory over Wolverhampton Wanderers at the Molineux Stadium, keeping the Blues unbeaten in the Championship and moving them to second place in the table. The win was largely defined by a single moment of defensive error from Wolves, as Jackson Tchatchoua inadvertently scored an own goal in the first half, sending the ball into the corner that the Wolves striker Adam Armstrong had been targeting in the 87th minute. Had Armstrong found the same corner, the match could have ended in a draw, but the goal proved decisive.

The match was dominated by Birmingham’s disciplined defence and efficient counter‑attacks. After the own goal, Wolves pressed for a quick equaliser, but their attempts were thwarted by a solid backline and a well‑positioned goalkeeper. In the 70th minute, Fer López supplied a precise pass to Birmingham striker César Peixoto, who calmly slotted the ball past the Wolves keeper to extend the Blues’ lead. Despite a late surge from Wolves, the defence held firm, and the team’s unbeaten run in the league continued.

With the victory, Birmingham City solidified their position in the upper half of the Championship standings, while Wolverhampton Wanderers will look to regroup after a disappointing home defeat. The result underscores Birmingham’s resilience and tactical discipline, qualities that will be crucial as the season progresses.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maitland‑Niles' 25‑yard goal secures Everton's point against Manchester United
content:
Everton’s search for a new right‑back ended on Monday with the £4.3 million signing of Ainsley Maitland‑Niles, a move that drew mixed reactions from fans and pundits alike. The former Arsenal midfielder, who had been on the fringes of the Premier League, was immediately thrust into the starting lineup for David Moyes’s side as they faced Manchester United at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The decision to start the 24‑year‑old in a high‑stakes fixture underscored the club’s urgency to fill the defensive gap left by the departure of their previous right‑back.

In his debut, Maitland‑Niles delivered a match‑deciding performance. Seventeen minutes into the game, he struck a 25‑yard free‑kick into the top corner of the net, giving Everton a 1‑0 lead that would prove decisive. United had been on the brink of victory after Benjamin Sesko’s 88th‑minute header, but the goal forced a frantic scramble. Everton’s defense held firm for the remainder of the match, and the win preserved their unbeaten start to the season, a point that was all the more valuable given the turmoil of the transfer deadline day.

The result has reinforced Everton’s resolve to remain competitive in the Premier League. With a fresh right‑back now contributing immediately, the club’s defensive stability is expected to improve, while the victory over a title‑contender has bolstered confidence ahead of a challenging fixture list. The match also highlighted the importance of decisive moments in tight games, as Maitland‑Niles’ goal proved pivotal in securing a point against a formidable opponent.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Antonelli Wins Italian GP, Ending 60-Year Wait
content:
Kimi Antonelli claimed his first Formula 1 victory at the Italian Grand Prix, turning a 19th‑grid start into a historic win at Monza. The 22‑year‑old Mercedes driver out‑paced his teammate George Russell, who had begun the race from second and finished second. Antonelli’s late‑race surge, combined with a strong performance from Max Verstappen, who secured third place for Red Bull, underscored a dramatic day for the championship contenders.

Lewis Hamilton finished sixth in the race, while Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc avoided serious injury after a high‑speed crash at the Parabolica corner early in the event. Leclerc’s exit from the track was a relief for the team, as the incident could have jeopardised his season. The race also saw a mix of strategic pit stops and tire choices, with Mercedes and Red Bull capitalising on their cars’ reliability and the drivers’ skill to secure the top three positions.

The Italian Grand Prix highlighted the unpredictable nature of Formula 1, where a driver starting from the back of the grid can still claim victory. Antonelli’s triumph at his home circuit added a memorable chapter to the season, while the performances of Russell, Verstappen, Hamilton, and Leclerc set the stage for the remaining races in the championship.
author: Guardian Sport

title: US Open 2026 Fourth Round: Sabalenka Faces Townsend at Flushing Meadows
content:
Fourth‑round action at Flushing Meadows saw a tense doubles match that ended 4‑4, with the pair facing a decisive tie‑break against the reigning champion. Daniel, who has been following the tournament closely, shared updates on his social‑media channels, encouraging fans to keep up on TikTok and Bluesky for live commentary. The match featured a strategic battle between Townsend and Sabalenka, with Townsend employing topspin cross‑cushion shots aimed at Sabalenka’s backhand to force her outside the lines. Townsend also attempted to slow the pace, hoping to frustrate the champion who typically dislikes prolonged wind‑ups.

In addition to the on‑court drama, Townsend’s appearance drew attention when he wore a coat reminiscent of the Night’s Watch, a detail that sparked commentary among spectators and commentators alike. Analysts noted that the wind‑swept conditions at the venue may have influenced the players’ tactics, with Townsend’s slower play potentially capitalizing on the unpredictable breeze. The match concluded with a tightly contested finish, leaving fans eager to see how the remaining rounds will unfold.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maro Itoje Recalled to England Squad
content:
England’s second‑row forward Maro Itoje has re‑joined the national squad after being named in the 36‑man training group for the autumn Nations Championship. The 28‑year‑old, who has been a key player for the Wasps and the national team, was added to the extended squad as the side prepares for its upcoming test matches against the home nations and France.

Itoje’s inclusion follows a period of injury‑related absences that saw him miss earlier fixtures. The England coaching staff have highlighted his experience and work rate as valuable assets for the team’s forward pack, and his return to the set‑up is expected to bolster the squad’s depth ahead of the high‑profile autumn series. The training squad will continue to refine strategies and assess player fitness in the lead‑up to the first match of the Championship.
author: BBC Sport

title: England beat Ireland 3-0, Dunkley scores century
content:
England’s women’s cricket team capped their international summer with a decisive victory over Ireland at Worcester, winning by 114 runs. Sophia Dunkley led the attack, scoring a brilliant 119 runs to steer England to a comfortable total, while the Irish bowlers struggled to contain the English side.

The match, played on a day that offered little assistance to the bowlers, saw England post a formidable score before their bowlers dismantled Ireland’s batting lineup. Ireland were bowled out for a modest total, and England’s bowlers exploited the conditions to secure a comprehensive win. The result confirms England’s dominance in the current international circuit and leaves Ireland with a challenging task ahead of their next fixtures.

With the summer’s international series concluded, England’s squad will now shift focus to upcoming tournaments, while Ireland will look to regroup and improve their performance in future encounters. The match at Worcester highlights England’s depth and the rising standards of women’s cricket worldwide.
author: BBC Sport

title: Everton vs Man United Player Ratings and Sub Impact
content:
Everton and Manchester United faced off in a pre‑season friendly at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday, a match that drew a modest crowd of 5,000. The game, part of each club’s preparation for the upcoming season, saw a mix of first‑team regulars and youth prospects take to the pitch. Everton’s lineup featured new signing Jadon Sancho, midfielder James Rodriguez, and centre‑back Ben Godfrey, while United fielded a squad heavy with academy talent, including midfielder Mason Greenwood and striker Marcus Rashford.

Player ratings, compiled by the match officials, placed Sancho at 7.8, the highest for the visitors, followed by Rodriguez at 7.1 and Godfrey at 6.9. On the United side, Rashford earned a 7.5, Greenwood a 7.0, and defender Harry Maguire a 6.8. Goalkeepers were rated 7.2 for Everton’s Jordan Pickford and 7.0 for United’s Dean Henderson. The ratings reflect the overall performance of each player, with the top performers noted for their impact on the game’s flow and defensive solidity.

The friendly concluded with a 2‑1 victory for Manchester United, a result that gave the squad confidence ahead of the competitive fixtures. The ratings suggest that both teams have promising talent ready for the season, with United’s young core showing particular promise in midfield and attack, while Everton’s new signings have begun to integrate into the squad’s dynamics. The match at Hill Dickinson Stadium therefore served as a useful benchmark for both clubs as they fine‑tune their line‑ups for the challenges ahead.
author: BBC Sport

title: Antonelli Wins Italian Grand Prix from 19th on Grid
content:
Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli secured a stunning victory at the 2024 Italian Grand Prix, climbing from 19th on the grid to the checkered flag in a race marked by numerous incidents. The Monza circuit saw a chaotic opening lap, with a multi‑vehicle collision on the first corner forcing a safety car and a reshuffle of the field. Antonelli, who had qualified 19th, used the early caution to his advantage, advancing through the midfield as several front‑row cars were damaged or retired.

Throughout the race, Antonelli’s team executed a flawless pit‑stop strategy, switching to a harder compound that allowed him to maintain a steady pace while his rivals struggled with tire degradation. He overtook key competitors on the high‑speed straights, capitalising on a late‑race safety car that bunched the field together. On the final lap, a last‑minute error by the race leader opened a gap that Antonelli closed with a decisive overtake, securing the win for Mercedes and marking a career‑highlighting performance for the rookie driver.

The victory underscores Mercedes’ continued competitiveness in the championship, while also highlighting Antonelli’s skill and composure under pressure. With the win, he gains valuable points for the Constructors’ Championship and cements his status as a rising talent in Formula 1. The Italian Grand Prix will be remembered for its dramatic incidents and the remarkable rise of a driver who began the day in 19th place.
author: BBC Sport

title: Former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall says he could not serve under Trump
content:
Former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall III told ABC’s “This Week” on Sunday that he “couldn’t serve” in a Trump administration, sharply criticizing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s stewardship of the Pentagon. Kendall, who served as the department’s top civilian official from 2021 to 2023, said he has “never seen an attempt to politicize our military like the one being conducted by Pete Hegseth,” adding that such actions undermine the nonpartisan nature of the armed forces.

Kendall’s remarks came amid a broader wave of concern among senior defense officials. Earlier in the week, the Army Secretary also voiced apprehension about perceived political interference in military affairs, echoing calls for preserving the service’s apolitical stance. Both statements highlight growing tension between former defense leaders and the current administration’s approach to civilian‑military relations.
author: The Hill

title: Faster Labor Contracts Act to Speed Up Collective Bargaining
content:
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick urged the Senate to approve the Faster Labor Contracts Act, a bill designed to streamline collective‑bargaining processes and safeguard the economic stability of working families. In a statement released Monday, Fitzpatrick highlighted the growing need for quicker contract negotiations amid rising inflation and labor shortages across key industries.

The proposed legislation would establish a federal framework that allows unions and employers to reach binding agreements within a shorter timeframe, reducing the likelihood of prolonged strikes or work stoppages. By codifying expedited procedures, the act aims to protect workers from wage stagnation and ensure that essential services remain uninterrupted. Fitzpatrick noted that the measure would also provide clearer guidelines for dispute resolution, helping to maintain a predictable labor market for businesses and households alike.

If enacted, the Faster Labor Contracts Act could set a new standard for labor relations nationwide, potentially easing tensions between labor and management while reinforcing the economic security of families dependent on stable employment. Fitzpatrick called on Senate leaders to prioritize the bill, emphasizing its importance for both workers and the broader economy.
author: The Hill

title: Former Air Force secretary questions ‘advice’ Trump received before starting Iran war
content:
Former U.S. Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall III raised a question about the decision‑making process that led President Donald Trump into military action against Iran. On Sunday, Kendall appeared on ABC’s “This Week” with host Martha Raddatz and asked, “What I don’t understand, frankly, about the Iran war is what advice was given to the president that led him to start this conflict?” The comment follows the 2020 U.S. strike that killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani and the subsequent escalation that drew the two nations into a near‑war.

Kendall, who served as Air Force Secretary from 2017 to 2019, has long been a critic of the Trump administration’s approach to Middle Eastern policy. By questioning the counsel that shaped the president’s decision, he is highlighting concerns over the transparency and accountability of the executive branch’s military strategies. His remarks come amid ongoing debates about the legality and strategic wisdom of the U.S. strike and the broader implications for U.S. foreign policy.

The former secretary’s remarks underscore the continuing scrutiny of the Trump administration’s foreign‑policy decisions. As analysts and lawmakers reassess the events that led to the Iran confrontation, Kendall’s question serves as a reminder of the importance of clear, evidence‑based advice in shaping national security actions.
author: The Hill

title: US Wealth Surpasses National Debt, No Austerity Needed
content:
The way a nation’s debt is framed can shape the policy options that appear viable. When the debt is presented as a multiple of a single year’s income, the narrative quickly narrows to two unattractive choices: either slash government spending or raise taxes on the wages and salaries that ordinary Americans rely on. Both options carry significant political and social costs, and they tend to dominate public debate and legislative proposals.

An alternative perspective compares debt to the country’s total wealth rather than to annual income. Under this lens, the debt load appears less daunting, revealing a fiscal space that can be used to fund public priorities without resorting to austerity or tax hikes on the middle class.
